newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 17.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - July 17.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

WMC Ltd said on Wednesday it was deferring a A$157 million expansion of its St Ives gold mine in Western Australia due to declines in the gold price. It also said production of nickel metal and matte by Australian mining house WMC Ltd suffered in 1996/97 (July/June) due to an accident at its Kalgoorlie smelter in April, WMC said on Wednesday. Production of nickel metal fell 17.5 percent to 9,027 tonnes in the quarter to June 30 versus the previous quarter, it said.
* Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd A$18.19 (-0.08)
Copper output from BHP and Rio Tinto's Escondida copper mine in Chile fell sharply to 74,006 tonnes in June from 119,997 tonnes in May and 66,912 in June 1996.

Sinclair Broadcast Group Inc. Wednesday said it agreed to buy 24 radio and six television stations from Heritage Media Group for $630 million in cash. The acquisition will occur when Heritage merges with News Corp. Ltd., which is expected to occur in the first quarter of 1998.

Broker First Pacific is expected to release a research report valuing C-C Amatil shares at about A$10.85 a share and was overvalued, trading currently at 45 times earnings, compared with the Coca Cola Co's 41 times earnings.

Australian listed group HIH Winterthur Insurance said on Thursday it had acquired all the shares in Colonial Mutual General Insurance NZ Ltd. The acquisition was made through Winterthur's New Zealand subsidiary, HIH Casualty and General Insurance NZ Ltd.

W.C. Penfold Ltd said on Thursday it has decided not to sell its 54.4 percent stake in Penfold Printing Ltd PPR.AX . The business supplies group also said that due to difficult retail trading conditions, it expected the W.C. Penfold group's profit result for the year to June 30 to be substantially down on the prior year.

Oil and gas junior Petroz NL said on Wednesday it had increased reserves for the Silver Springs/Renlim fields in the Surat Basin following a pilot dewatering project. Proven and probable reserves of sales gas had increased by 16 petajoules, condensate by 500,000 standard barrels and liquid petroleum gas by 75,000 tonnes, Petroz said.
